clue.text: Very posh urban areas cover extremely hard English hills

parts.note: very means so, as in 'so tired'
U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage

indicators.note: the towns are wrapped round the next piece, covering it

parts.note: urban areas are towns

indicators.note: extremely asks for the letters at each extreme of the word hard

explanation.surface: Smart suburbs are spreading over the rugged hills of southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: The South Downs are a range of chalk hills in southern England; 'extremely' takes only the outside letters of 'hard', which 'cover' places within the towns.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Downs are a well-known chalk range running across Sussex and Hampshire, a set of English hills.

clue.text: Attendants in St Edward's ignore first duke

indicators.note: ignore first tells us to leave out the earliest occurrence of the following letter

parts.note: the name written out, apostrophe dropped, gives these letters

explanation.surface: Ushers at a school or church called St Edward's are told to overlook the senior aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: St Edward's has two Ds; 'ignore first' removes only the earlier one, leaving the second in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewards are people who attend to guests or passengers, so they are attendants.

clue.text: Prudent father escorting girl around university

indicators.note: the pair goes around the next letter, enclosing it between them
escorting means going alongside, so father and girl sit side by side

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A careful dad accompanies his daughter on a tour of the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escorting' joins father and girl, and 'around' makes the pair enclose the university letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Frugal means sparing with money, which is what a prudent spender is.

clue.text: Comparatively little or no working at end of class

indicators.note: no here means without, signalling that the next piece is taken away
at end of says the removed letters come from the end of the longer word

parts.note: a class at school is a lesson
working means on, as in a machine being on

explanation.surface: A pupil complains of hardly any work being done as the class finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' and 'at end of' take ON (working) off the end of LESSON (class).
explanation.definitionFit: Less is the comparative of little, meaning a smaller amount than another.

clue.text: Sadat supported illegal act in conflict in '50s

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporter sits below, so Sadat's name goes under the illegal act

parts.note: an illegal act is a crime
Anwar Sadat was President of Egypt

explanation.surface: An Egyptian president backed some wrongdoing during a 1950s war.
explanation.walkthrough: '50s' suggests the 1950s, Sadat's own era and the Suez crisis, but the Crimean War was fought in the 1850s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War of 1853 to 1856 was a conflict fought in the 1850s.

clue.text: Check crew for someone acting dangerously

parts.note: to stunt is to check growth
to crew a ship is to man it

explanation.surface: A film director checks the team before a risky scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuntman performs dangerous action scenes in place of an actor, literally acting at risk.

clue.text: Cheap move by Tory leader

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly

indicators.note: leader asks for the first letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief makes a penny-pinching manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Budget used as an adjective describes low-cost goods, such as a budget airline, so it means inexpensive.

clue.text: Corner shop starts to save pennies and retrench

indicators.note: starts to asks for the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A local convenience store begins cutting costs to save money.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAR is a chain of convenience stores, the typical British corner shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Spar is the brand name of a chain of small convenience stores, an example of a neighbourhood shop.

clue.text: He exposes river in Ulster, say

parts.note: someone who outs or exposes others is an outer
the Wear is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: A man reveals a river in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster' looks like the Irish province but is a long heavy overcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long loose overcoat, so it is an example of a garment worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Hit, he departs, sulking

indicators.note: departs says the letters of he leave the phrase

parts.note: someone sulking has the hump, British slang for being in a bad mood
taken as written

explanation.surface: He walks out in a sulk after being struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hump' is British slang for a sulky mood; 'departs' removes the HE from THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To thump someone is to strike them hard with the fist, which is to hit.

clue.text: Fibres no good as fuel

parts.note: tow is the coarse broken fibre of flax or hemp
taken as written

explanation.surface: Worthless fibres are used for burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Town gas was gas made from coal and piped to homes for heating and cooking, a fuel.

clue.text: A Frenchman and a German jointly guard boss

indicators.note: the two together guard, so the Frenchman and the German enclose the other pieces between them

parts.note: M is the abbreviation of Monsieur, a Frenchman
taken as written
N is a short form of and, as in rock 'n' roll
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two foreign security men team up to protect their employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jointly guard' puts ANA (A, N for 'and', A) between M and GER, the two together forming the guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager is the person in charge, so is a boss.

clue.text: Double over radius of membrane

indicators.note: over here says the double goes over the radius, covering it on both sides

parts.note: dual means double, twofold
R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: Twice the radius of a thin layer of tissue is being measured.
explanation.definitionFit: Dural is the adjective from dura, the tough outer membrane around the brain, so it means relating to that tissue.

clue.text: Hard-nosed paper probes impact at sea

indicators.note: the paper probes, pushing into the middle of the other letters
at sea means confused, so the letters of impact are muddled

parts.note: rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A tough tabloid investigates the effect of something offshore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like part of the picture but signals the anagram; 'probes' sends the paper into the jumbled letters just after their first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pragmatic means practical and unsentimental, the same as a hard-nosed approach.

clue.text: It's wasteful of girl shakily filling noggin

indicators.note: filling says the next letters are packed inside the head

parts.note: noggin is informal for the head, as is pate

indicators.note: shakily means the letters of 'of girl' are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wasteful remark about a girl unsteadily topping up a small mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noggin' suggests a small drinking cup but means head; 'shakily' jumbles 'of girl' and 'filling' puts the result inside the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate spender is recklessly extravagant, which is wasteful.

clue.text: Cold returns anew, squeezing company to reduce quality

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: the rearranged letters squeeze the company in among them
anew asks for the letters of returns made over in fresh order

explanation.surface: Chilly weather comes back once more, pinching a business into lowering standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' looks like a verb about the weather but is anagram fodder for 'anew'; 'squeezing' traps the company within the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut corners is an idiom for doing something cheaply or hastily, at the cost of quality.

clue.text: Santa went to town, spreading advice on economy

indicators.note: spreading scatters the letters of the phrase into a new order

explanation.surface: Father Christmas went all out, giving tips on saving.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb urges thrift: avoid wasting anything and you will never be short, which is guidance on saving.

clue.text: Boy brought in moth in kitchen device that's been pinched

indicators.note: brought in means the boy is put inside the moth's name

parts.note: the egger, or eggar, is a kind of moth
Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A child brings a moth into the kitchen, and something there has been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched' looks like stolen but describes the narrow waist of an hourglass-shaped timer.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg timer is a small sand glass for timing boiled eggs, narrowed in the middle.

clue.text: The North is investing Republic's money, creating disorder

indicators.note: investing means wrapping round, so the north and is enclose the money

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north
taken as written
the Irish Republic's currency is the euro, here plural

explanation.surface: The North puts the Irish Republic's cash into a scheme that causes chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' wants to be about finance; here it means clothing, so N and IS surround EUROS.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder marked by anxiety or obsession.

clue.text: Bowl over, bringing sides in separately for tail-ender

indicators.note: bringing with in says the side letters are carried into the other word
in with bringing says the side letters are carried into the other word
separately says the two side letters enter at different points rather than together

parts.note: to bowl someone over is to stagger them, amaze them
R stands for right, one of the two sides
L stands for left, the other of the two sides

explanation.surface: A cricketer knocks over a low-order batsman, with both sides involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'separately' tells you R and L go in at different points: ST R AGG L ER. 'Bowl' and 'tail-ender' suggest cricket, where a tail-ender is a weak batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A straggler lags behind the rest, so comes at the tail end of a group.

clue.text: Again employed trick, taking in Spain and Germany

indicators.note: taking in says the trick holds the following letter inside it

parts.note: a ruse is a trick
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A scheme involving two European countries is used once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts E inside RUSE after the R; D for Germany follows on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Reused means put to use a second time, which is employed again.

clue.text: Place ring round large dog

indicators.note: round says these letters go around the next one

parts.note: to place is to put
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
a ring is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Set a collar round a big hound.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto is the Disney cartoon dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's pet in Disney cartoons, a famous cartoon dog.

clue.text: Drag over to table in Washington

indicators.note: over here means the puff goes over the word to, covering it

parts.note: a drag on a cigarette is a puff
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes a puff on a cigarette before going to a meeting in the US capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage, to table a motion is to postpone it, whereas in Britain it means to put it forward.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English tabling a motion means deferring it, the same as putting it off.

clue.text: Police initially arrest head of garden for job he does

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word Police

parts.note: to run in is informal for arresting someone

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word garden

explanation.surface: A head gardener's task involves officers picking someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'head of garden': 'he' is the gardener the clue has just mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting back plants is a routine task for a gardener, so it is a job he does.

clue.text: I have no idea how to succeed in exam

definitions.meaning: said by a quiz contestant who cannot answer a question
to get through a test successfully

explanation.surface: A student says they have no idea how to get through a test.
explanation.definitionFit: In a quiz you say the word when you don't know the answer, and you get through an exam by achieving that result.

clue.text: Drunk lecturer guzzling whiskey fell

parts.note: cut is British slang for drunk

indicators.note: guzzling means taking in, so the lecturer swallows the next letter

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An inebriated academic downing spirits falls over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like the past of 'fall' but is the verb meaning to bring down a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To fell a tree is to chop it to the ground, the same as cutting it down.

clue.text: Restrain rookie trapping rook

indicators.note: trapping says the rookie holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: a cub is a beginner, as in a cub reporter
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: Keep a novice from capturing a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb something is to hold it in check, the same as restraining it.

clue.text: Riddle: divide 7 minus n by 1

indicators.note: divide by says the next piece splits the word, sitting inside it
minus tells us to take away the letter that follows it

parts.note: the number seven written out
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle asks you to divide seven minus n by one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' is a puzzle, but here is a coarse sieve; the arithmetic is wordplay. 'minus' takes the last N from SEVEN; 'divide' splits SEVE with I.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a coarse sieve used for sifting soil or gravel, and to riddle is to sift.

clue.text: Husband split during row, more 3

indicators.note: during means within, so the husband and split go inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
a rift is a split

explanation.surface: A couple separate during a quarrel over saving money.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to the answer at 3 down, FRUGAL; 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: Thriftier means more careful with money, the comparative of the word in 3 down.
